Conceptual spine

The AI-native SDLC

The familiar lifecycle remains useful. What changes is the speed of production and the evidence needed to trust each transition.

THE CENTRAL SHIFT

Trust moves to the record.

When agents produce code quickly, human review capacity and reliable handoffs become the constraint. Each stage must leave a durable artifact for the next seat.

Why it changes

Code stopped being the scarce part.

Traditional delivery assumes implementation consumes most of the effort. Agentic work changes that balance. Planning, context, review, and acceptance can become the slower parts of the system.

The answer is not to remove human judgment. It is to make each human gate smaller and better informed by giving it a committed artifact, an independent check, and a clear decision.

The conceptual source is Anthropic’s AI-Native SDLC Playbook ↗. The DataCraft implementation adds persistent project management, Ringer gates, and replaceable CLI workers.

Six-stage loop

  1. 01 · JOE + HERMES

    Plan

    State the outcome, constraints, users, and open questions.

    intent.md
  2. 02 · PM

    Design

    Resolve the behavior, boundaries, and acceptance conditions.

    spec.md
  3. 03 · CLI WORKERS

    Build

    Execute bounded tasks in dependency order.

    plan + code
  4. 04 · RINGER

    Test

    Run the declared checks and capture the result independently.

    evidence + receipt
  5. 05 · PM + HUMAN

    Deploy

    Accept the revision and apply consequential production changes.

    delivery record
  6. 06 · HERMES

    Maintain

    Observe issues, diagnose failures, and feed learning into new intent.

    issue → intent
THE ARTIFACT CHAINEach transition leaves something inspectable.
intent→spec→diff→receipt→acceptance↺
